senses.sense: The inward worker in man that digests food and separates the pure from the impure; called the inborn Chymist God planted in man, whose instrument is the stomach; each of stomach, liver and kidneys has one.

evidence.quote: ariseth out of the last matter of the Meat by the Archaeus, or digestion of the Stomack
the Stomack which is the instrument of Mans Archaeus, or the Internal, innate Chymist which God hath planted in Man
But if the Archaeus of our stomack, liver or kidneys, which separateth the pure from the impure be infected
Therefore the Archaeus of the stomack must destroy the Tartar of the Elements least it be turned into the Tartar of Man

senses.sense: The Art of Nature: the inward power that heals the body, to which the cure may be left without any medicine.

evidence.quote: the sole Archaeus or Art of Nature

senses.sense: One Spirit with Astrum and Vulcanus, without Reason, and differing as the forms of things differ (margin note only).

evidence.quote: Astrum, Vulcanus and Archaeus are the same thing, & but one Spirit yet without Reason

senses.sense: Faith in God, the faith of grace by Christ, by which eternal things are seen; named as the foundation of physick.

evidence.quote: Eternall things are to be seen onely by Faith
I speak not of the Faith of Grace by Christ
The best and chiefest Foundation of Physick is faith in God, and love to our neighbour

senses.sense: Faith as a working power: it does in the manner of spirits what the body does visibly, gives the Imagination, commands creatures, and alone resists diseases of the mind; the text says it is the work of him in whom we believe.

evidence.quote: What we doe visiby by the body, that doe we by Faith after the manner of Spirits
Faith is at least a work, I mean his work in whom we believe.
when we think, and have faith in our cogitations, then faith doth the work, but without faith we can doe nothing
Faith giveth the Imagination
every creature is at the beck and command of their faith who are men innocent and taught in the Law of the Lord
No corporall guard or shelter availeth any thing against such like violences, but onely Faith which is able to resist them

senses.sense: The sick man's trust in the physician and his physick, which helps toward health.

evidence.quote: A firm Faith, undoubted Hope, Love and Confidence toward the Physitian and his Physick, doth very much conduce to health

senses.sense: The drawing stone itself, used in plaisters and named as a likeness for things that attract or work invisibly.

evidence.quote: by application of drawing Plaisters made of the Load-stone and other things
As the Earthy Load stone in its body is a spirit and draweth to it selfe
The Imagination or Fantasie of Man is like the Load stone in its Nature, attracting the Fantasie of other men
those wonderfull vertues in the Nature of the Antipathicall Loadstone, which doth (as it were) bewitch spiritually and invisibly

senses.sense: The sydereall spirit in man, born of the Astra's and united to them, which draws their force into him: the Load stone of the Microcosm.

evidence.quote: This sydereall Spirit which is born of the Astra's together with Man (and therefore remains united to the Astra's) is the Load stone and hath a magnetick nature in man.
this is the Load stone of the Microcosm
The sydereall body and spirit attract unto them the force of the Astra's

senses.sense: God's creating word FIAT (Let there be), by which the first matter, heaven and earth and all things were brought out of darkness into light.

evidence.quote: By the word FIAT (or Let there be) God produced the first matter
by this Word, FIAT, the seed of the whole world, were Heaven and Earth created
were called out to the visible Light by the WORD speaking, and the Spirit cherishing
by vertue of that omnipotent Word, whereby all things were brought out of darknesse into Light

senses.sense: The WORD of God as the heavenly medicine that alone heals all things: incarnate, found in the creatures, giving medicines their force, and not known to every one; herbs are only its sign.

evidence.quote: The Caelestiall Medicine onely, or the WORD of God
hearbs are not the medicines, but a signe onely of the Word signified
he did it by One Word, and he is that Word, to wit, the increated Mercy of God
Physitians also have wrought great cures by the Created Word, or the incarnate Mercy
This Word then is the true medicine that healeth all things, but is not known to every one
the WORD of God INCARNATE which may be found in the Creatures
that is he doth performe it in the WONDERFULL WORD by the Mind, Faith and Prayer

senses.sense: Words spoken, written or carved as means of cure: invisible bodies, as medicines are visible ones.

evidence.quote: Medicines are visible bodies; Words are invisible bodies
Concerning Characteristicalll Cure which affecteth Naturall operations by words pronounced, written, carved and hanged about the neck
by a Word written and Characters or Signes

spellings: Soule or Spirit of the world

senses.sense: The universal spirit that lives in, quickens and fills the whole world, a united life knitting all things together.

evidence.quote: That universall Spirit which liveth in and quickneth this whole Masse, which worketh all in all, and filleth the whole world
The Soule of the world is a kind of united life, filling, gathering and knitting together all things
the magnetick spark of the Soule of the world liveth and worketh effectually

senses.sense: Avicen's name for that universal spirit, as poured into all things; the author adds that this is to be heard without superstition.

evidence.quote: Avicen saith, it is the Soule of the world powred into all things

senses.sense: The matter of which the chief Medicine is made, holding the force of all heavenly and earthly things.

evidence.quote: this Medicine is made of the more incorruptible and efficacious Matter that can be under Heaven, that is, the Soule or Spirit of the world

senses.sense: The fourth kind of Naturall Magick, which by Art does invisibly and spiritually what Nature does visibly and bodily without that help.

evidence.quote: This fourth kind of Naturall Magick called Gamahaea doth all things invisibly and spiritually, by the help of Art, which Nature is able to doe visibly and corporally without such help.

senses.sense: The powerful impression by which characters and stones cure: a wedlock of heavenly influence to an earthly sign, joining superiors and inferiors.

evidence.quote: by Characters and Stones with a most powerfull impression, to wit, the Gamahaea of Influentiall Wedlock to the Terrestiall signe, by matrimoniall combination of the Superiors and Inferiors ASTRALLY

senses.sense: An inborn faith or wisdom God the Father gave equally to all men at the Creation, distinct from the faith of grace by Christ; the text says it is our Imagination, and that it can cause and cure diseases.

evidence.quote: Secondly, by NATURALL FAITH, or in-born Wisdome, which God the Father equally communicated to all men in the Creation
Naturall Faith (I speak not of the Faith of Grace by Christ) inborn of God the Father in the first Creation, which is our IMAGINATION, is so powerfull that it can both cause and cure diseases
Againe, the aforesaid Naturall Faith its efficacy manifested it selfe in the woman that had the bloody issue, and in the Centurion.
the efficacy of the faith of Nature, which by God can do all things Naturally

senses.sense: A change of a body or substance into another state: of one's own or another's body by a vehement imagination, of the Salt in man, whose change decides the disease, and of things of natural composition, which are subject to it.

evidence.quote: A vehement Imagination doth not onely cause a transmutation of ones own body, but sometimes also of anothers
Which Salt may be changed and turned into all sorts of Salts, and such as is the Transmutation such also is the disease.
are subject to corruption and transmutation

senses.sense: Something the Sulphur gives to bodies, beside substance; the lines do not say more. Interpreted narrowly: the body's capacity to change.

evidence.quote: The Sulphur by a pleasant mixture tempereth the coagulation of the Salt, and gives the Body Substance and Transmutation

senses.sense: Physicians the author counts as of his own kind: named among them are Quercetan, Bovius and Muffet, who answered the adversaries of Paracelsean physick; their custom is to pray for a blessing on their work.

evidence.quote: my honoured friend Joseph Quercetan Councellour and most worthy Physitian to the King of France, by Th: Bovius an Italian of Verona, and Th: Muffet an Englishman, the best Hermetick Physitians of this age
imitate that most commendable and religious custome of the Hermetick Physitians, who always use to pray for a blessing upon their endeavours

senses.sense: The perfect part of a sublunary thing, which fire can separate from its dregs, the imperfect part.

evidence.quote: a perfect and an imperfect, that is, a fift Essence and the dreggs may be separated one from the other by fire

senses.sense: The chief Medicine: the purer essence of the four Elements, made equal in it, which God created as the root of life to preserve the human body, as Heaven preserves the universe; incorruptible and of the nature of Heaven.

evidence.quote: The most High created this Fift Essence as the root of life in Nature for the preservation of the four qualities of the Humane body
the Fift Essence of the whole frame of the world, and the whole world Regenerated
the Fift Essence or Fift Virtue resulting from the purer Essence of the four Elements
that Fift Essence of the Human Body bindeth the Elements or Humors in Peace and Harmonicall league
in this Fift Essence and Spirituall Medicine, which hath the Nature and Heat of Heaven
The Tincture is the Fife Essence of the Microcosm
have called this Fist Essence the middle nature of Soules

senses.sense: The same, as the reason the philosophers of Hermes' school give: compounded of the four Elements, all of them actually in it.
senses.voice: QUOTED: Phylosophers our predecessors that have been train'd up in Hermes school

evidence.quote: the Fift Essence compounded of the four Elements, in which are all the Elements actually

senses.sense: Occult qualities the Soul of the world infuses into things to make them fruitful, commonly so called (margin note only).

evidence.quote: occult qualities which are commonly called the Fift Effences

senses.sense: Mercury, Sulphur and Salt, the three into which every natural body is resolved and of which it is made; their spirits work in natural actions, and diseases spring from their spirits and from their exaltation or loss of proportion.

evidence.quote: there are THREE Principles of all things which are found in every compound body
No body compos'd by Nature can by any dissolving skill be parted into more or lesse then Three, viz. Into Mercury or liquor, Sulphur or Oyle, and Salt
the mecanick sciences of the Three principles have their vigour
from the Nature of the Seed or Astra's and Invisible mechanick Spirits of the Three principles
the Naturall proportion of the Three First (or as common Physitians say, the disorder and ill disposition of the four Elements or Humors)
the diseases that hapned by the exaltation of the Three Principles

senses.sense: The chymist's dissolving of a body by art, which brings to light the properties that lay in its composition and brings a thing's power into act.

evidence.quote: By this artificall resolution of bodyes the propertyes which before layd in the compositions of them are now brought to light.
as in a Spagiricall resolution is plainly to be seen
had its power reduced into act by a Naturall and due Resolution, that it might exercise its vertues

senses.sense: A dissolving inside the body: one of the ways the Salt destroys health, the turning of salt into urine, and the joining of the medicine with the nutriment.

evidence.quote: Salt destroyeth health 4 wayes, by Resolution, Calcination
forced into resolution by the violence of separation
which is done by resolution and conjuction with the Nutriment

senses.sense: The resolution of the Iliad, a cause of death the physician's industry may hinder, set against death from the Ens; the lines do not say what the Iliad is.

evidence.quote: Therefore Paracelsus saith that the death which is from the resolution of the Iliad may be hindred by the industry of the Physitian, but that which is from the Ens or Being cannot

senses.sense: An outward thing that points to a hidden thing signified and is less than it: herbs are only a sign of the Word.

evidence.quote: hearbs are not the medicines, but a signe onely of the Word signified
Grace exceedeth Nature, and the thing signified excelleth the signe

senses.sense: A sign in heaven under which a creature or man is born.

evidence.quote: every living Creature hath its Ascendant signe in Heaven
who were born in a happy signe

senses.sense: An outward token of a disease, not the disease itself.

evidence.quote: those Accidents and Excrements are but the signes of the disease, and not the disease it selfe

senses.sense: A written or earthly sign that receives heavenly influence, named with characters in magical cure.

evidence.quote: by a Word written and Characters or Signes
the Gamahaea of Influentiall Wedlock to the Terrestiall signe

senses.sense: Written marks or signs, framed at a certain time by the power of Heaven, by which true magicians and the Magus cure, sooner than the physician by herbs.

evidence.quote: by a Word written and Characters or Signes
framed at a certaine time according to the power of Heaven, far from all superstition
performeth suddenly and much sooner by Characters and Stones with a most powerfull impression

senses.sense: Characters or constellated Names, whose force comes not from their figure or pronunciation but from the office God or Nature ordained to them.

evidence.quote: For Characters or constellated Names according to Agrippa, have no force from the Figureors Pronunciation, but by reason of the Vertue or Office which God or Nature hath ordained to such a Name or Character

senses.sense: Marks in minerals that disclose their hidden vertue to enlightened men and instructed philosophers.

evidence.quote: Thus also among Mineralls there Magicall and Hieroglyphicall Characters
that doe sufficiently insinuate to Inlightned men, and Magically disclose their hidden vertue to those more secret Phylosophers that are instructed therein

senses.sense: A rebirth to be sought before all natural things, which then come without much labour; called the field of heavenly physick that heals with a word. Interpreted narrowly: the regeneration the margin names as the ground of all sciences.

evidence.quote: The New Birth is the Field of Caelestiall Physick which healeth with a word without Externall means
Wherefore the New Birth is first to be sought for, and then all other Naturall things will be added without much labour.
All Sciences are perfectly attained unto by the Fundamentall of Faith and new Regeneration or Celestiall Transplantation

senses.sense: One of the two Lights, the light of theology, set beside the Light of Nature: it begets a true theologer, physick rises from it, and by it come eternal life and the inward vision of God.

evidence.quote: It taketh its rise from Theology or the Light of Grace, and endeth in the Light of Nature.
The Light of Grace, begetteth a true Theologer, yet not without Phylosophy
The two Lights are well known, within which are all thing, without which is nothing
by the supernall help of the Light of Grace we may together with Christ and all the Elect possesse that Eternall Life
which also hapneth by the Light of Grace to the separate Soul even in this world
which Treasures are to be manifest indifferently to all in due time by the light of Grace and Nature
make manifest the Light of GRACE and NATURE
